messages:
alex: Well this morning the compiler flirted with my code and optimized my bug away. I'm both relieved and betrayed. :sweat_smile:
maya: haha same. optimizer: 'I loved you unconditionally until I couldn't prove you mattered.' :laughing:
jordan: pro tip: if your bug disappears in opt build, it's now an 'emergent feature'—document it in release notes.
ci-bot: [CI] build/test (opt) failed on commit abc123 - undefined-behavior sanitizer flagged. :warning:
alex: @maya you ever get a bug that only shows up when you add logging? feels like the code is shy.
maya: yup. logging = social anxiety for processes. sometimes I write `printf("I'm lonely\n");` and it works.
jordan: here's a harmless-looking UB snippet that creates art:
```
int* p = NULL;
printf("%c", *p);
```
alex: don't actually run that lol :facepalm:
sam: can we make a new sticker? 'I lost a bug to -O3 and all I got was optimized out' :stuck_out_tongue:
maya: +1. put it next to 'YAML: the whitespace cult' sticker.
ci-bot: [deploy-bot] note: rolling back to -O0 for the canary that's laughing at us.
jordan: moral of the story: if it only fails in optimized builds, it's either UB, undefined intentions, or your algorithm is playing hard-to-get.
alex: agreed. coffee and sanitizers for everyone? ☕️
maya: ☕️☕️☕️
sam: :tada:
